info.title: Yogabase Runtime Host API
info.description: Instance-only runtime-host lifecycle contract (roadmap D2). Calls are made by (or on behalf of) a single running runtime-host instance and by the Control Plane-side allocator; human administration, delivery, and application traffic are deliberately outside this contract. The whole surface ships fail-closed: until the compiled runtime-host qualification evidence is accepted, every route answers 503 RUNTIME_HOST_UNAVAILABLE. Compatibility policy is N/N-1: when a v2 of this contract is published, v1 remains served for at least one release cycle so SDK families can migrate without a flag day.

fleetRelay.description: The member's outbound mutually authenticated fleet session relay. Instances never dial the Control Plane directly and hold no Kubernetes or cloud credentials.

post.summary: Renew the instance's bounded health lease.
post.description: Heartbeats carry a strictly increasing client sequence; a replayed or reordered sequence is rejected with RUNTIME_HOST_STALE_SEQUENCE and does not renew the lease. A heartbeat from Starting or Unknown recovers the instance to Healthy — never directly to Ready, because readiness always requires accepted evidence. Lease durations are clamped to the 5 second – 5 minute contract bounds. A lease that expires moves the instance to Unknown, withdraws readiness, and voids any reservation; expiry never implies deletion — deletion requires an explicit tombstone bound to the exact resource UID.

post.summary: Request readiness; granted only with accepted member-observation evidence.
post.description: Ready is a request, not a self-declaration. The transition is granted only from Healthy and only after the Control Plane has accepted independent member-observation readiness evidence for this exact instance incarnation; otherwise the call fails with RUNTIME_HOST_READINESS_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED and the instance stays Healthy.

post.summary: Place a bounded reservation on a Ready instance.
post.description: A reservation holds a Ready instance for an imminent allocation for a bounded window (1 second – 10 minutes). Reservations are renewable while unexpired; an expired reservation returns the instance to Ready on the next observation. Reservation is Control Plane-authoritative — the instance cannot reserve itself into allocation.

post.summary: Begin an auditable drain toward shutdown.
post.description: Shutdown starts a drain: readiness is withdrawn immediately, existing work continues inside a bounded drain window (at most 30 minutes), and the completion event records whether the drain finished on its own (drain-complete) or was forced at the deadline (drain-deadline-forced). The request is idempotent. Deletion of the underlying workload still requires an explicit tombstone bound to the exact resource UID; this API never deletes.

get.summary: Read the instance's append-only assignment event stream.
get.description: The polling fallback and the resume path are the same read: events are append-only with a per-instance monotonic sequence, the resume token is the last sequence the caller has processed, and a page returns at most 100 events with the next resume token. Replaying a token re-delivers the same events in the same order — consumers must be idempotent. A malformed or non-monotonic token fails with RUNTIME_HOST_RESUME_TOKEN_INVALID rather than silently restarting the stream.

parameters.name: resumeToken
parameters.description: The last processed event sequence, exactly as returned by a previous page. Omit to read from the beginning.

post.summary: Allocate a Ready (or validly Reserved) instance, idempotently.
post.description: Allocation is Control Plane-authoritative and idempotent: replaying the same idempotency key with the same constraints digest returns the original allocation with replayed=true; the same key with different constraints fails with RUNTIME_HOST_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. A concurrent double-allocation of one instance is fenced by optimistic concurrency and surfaces as a retryable RUNTIME_HOST_ALREADY_ALLOCATED. When no Ready instance exists for the target the call fails with RUNTIME_HOST_NO_READY_INSTANCE instead of queueing. The response carries only the instance's registered non-secret connection metadata.

200.description: The allocation, freshly placed or idempotently replayed.

post.description: Releasing is idempotent; releasing an already-released allocation succeeds without effect. The instance returns toward Ready through its normal observed lifecycle — release never deletes anything.

runtimeHostBinding.name: Yogabase-Runtime-Host-Binding
runtimeHostBinding.description: Strict JSON envelope {"podUid":"...","workloadGeneration":N,"sessionEpoch":N} binding every call to one exact instance incarnation. A stale sessionEpoch, wrong podUid, or wrong workloadGeneration is rejected with 403 — a replaced Pod can never act as its predecessor. This surface accepts no delivery bearer token, no application credential, and no Kubernetes or cloud credential; production calls arrive only through the member's outbound mutually authenticated fleet session, which supplies the transport identity.

InstanceId.name: instanceId
InstanceId.description: The Control Plane-issued runtime-host instance identifier.

Lease.description: The instance's current lease and lifecycle position.

Unavailable.description: Runtime hosting is honestly unavailable: the compiled qualification gate is false because the enabling ADR is not accepted and the five-SDK conformance plus real-EKS exit has not passed.

ValidationProblem.description: The request body, resume token, or a bounded field is invalid.

BindingProblem.description: The instance binding envelope is missing, malformed, or names a stale incarnation (stale sessionEpoch, wrong podUid, wrong workloadGeneration, or a stale heartbeat sequence).

NotFoundProblem.description: The instance or allocation does not exist in this scope.

TransitionProblem.description: The lifecycle refuses the transition from the instance's honest current state (for example already allocated, no ready instance, shutdown in progress, or an idempotency conflict).

sequence.description: Strictly increasing client heartbeat sequence; replays and reordering are rejected.

seconds.description: Requested reservation window in seconds, within the 1 second – 10 minute contract bounds.

targetId.description: The member target whose Ready instances are eligible.

idempotencyKey.description: Caller-chosen replay key. The same key with the same constraints replays the original allocation; different constraints under the same key conflict.

constraintsJson.description: Bounded JSON allocation constraints; digested for idempotency comparison.

instanceId.description: Optional: allocate this exact instance (it must be Ready or validly Reserved) instead of letting the Control Plane pick.

eventSequence.description: The instance's latest assignment-event sequence; usable as a resume token.

kind.description: Audit event kind, for example registered, allocated, released, drain-complete, or drain-deadline-forced.

resumeToken.description: Pass back verbatim to continue after the last event in this page.

connectionMetadataJson.description: The instance's registered non-secret connection metadata. Registration rejects secret-looking material, so no credential can transit this field.

replayed.description: True when this response replays an earlier allocation under the same idempotency key.

RuntimeHostState.description: The nine-state runtime-host lifecycle. Unknown means the lease expired and the Control Plane makes no claim about the process; it never implies deletion.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 problem document with Yogabase extensions.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Present only on a retryable refusal, currently RUNTIME_HOST_INSTANCE_PENDING. How long to wait before repeating the identical call. The relay hop carries a status and a body and no headers, so this is the wire's Retry-After.

RuntimeHostErrorCode.description: RUNTIME_HOST_INSTANCE_PENDING is the one retryable member: it is answered 503 while the member's readiness observation for this Pod incarnation is still in flight, and the identical call succeeds once it arrives. Every other member is terminal for the call that produced it. RUNTIME_HOST_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND is reserved for a caller that names an instance directly; a self-scoped call over the Pod-local relay never receives it, because the Pod binding is stamped by the member, not asserted by the workload.
